issues.title: agent list returns "Backend unreachable" without auto-starting server

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Run ./b4w.ps1 agent list when the backend is not running.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The daemon should auto-start the backend (per documentation: "the first ./b4w.ps1 command will start the daemon and backend automatically") or prompt the user to start it.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Output says "Note: Backend unreachable — showing cached statuses. Start the server for live status." No attempt to auto-start the server. Only write commands like `agent run` trigger auto-start.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: Read-only commands (agent list, agent status) use a cached/local path that does not trigger the backend auto-start logic. Write commands (agent run) do trigger it. The auto-start guard is likely gated on whether the command requires a live backend connection.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Auto-start the backend on ANY command that needs it, not just write commands
- If auto-start is intentionally avoided for read commands (to keep them fast), at minimum display a hint like "Run any write command (e.g. agent run) to auto-start the backend"
- Document which commands trigger auto-start vs which don't

issues.title: No agent lifecycle documentation in SKILL.md — only command reference

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Read skills/browser4-cli/SKILL.md. Search for guidance on the agent lifecycle (run → status → result workflow with polling).

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: A section explaining the agent task lifecycle: how to submit a task, how to poll for status, how to retrieve results, what the status codes mean, and when to check isDone.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The SKILL.md mentions agent commands only in the Command Map table (line 146: "agent.md" reference) and lists them under "Agent:" in the help output. There is no lifecycle workflow section, no polling guidance, no status code reference, and no explanation of the JSON fields returned by agent status.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The SKILL.md delegates all agent documentation to references/agent.md without providing even a minimal quick-start lifecycle pattern in the main skill file.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Add an "Agent Lifecycle" section to SKILL.md with a minimal copy-paste template: agent run → poll agent status → agent result
- Include a table of common statusCode values (102=processing, 200=OK, 417=expectation failed, etc.)
- Document the isDone polling pattern explicitly
- Link to references/agent.md for full details

issues.title: Hint message uses wrong CLI invocation name for local development

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Run ./b4w.ps1 agent run "<task>" and observe the hint message.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Hint should reference the same invocation method the user is currently using (./b4w.ps1) or use a generic variable like $(b4w).

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Hint says: "Use 'browser4-cli agent status <id>' to check progress, or 'browser4-cli agent list' to view all tracked tasks." — this references the globally-installed CLI name, not the local ./b4w.ps1 the user is running.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The hint text is hardcoded with the global CLI name 'browser4-cli' and does not detect or adapt to the local invocation path being used.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Detect the actual argv[0] or script path used and substitute it into hints
- Or use a neutral form like "Use 'agent status <id>' to check progress" since users are already within the CLI context

issues.title: --help agent category not listed in category filter help text

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Run ./b4w.ps1 help and observe the category filter line: "Filter help by category: --help nav | --help extract | --help session | --help kb | --help swarm | --help crawl". Then run ./b4w.ps1 --help agent — it works but is not advertised.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: "--help agent" should appear in the list of available category filters.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: "--help agent" is functional but missing from the advertised category filter list. Similarly, "--help agent" is not mentioned in the SKILL.md reference.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The agent command family was likely added after the category filter list was authored, and the filter list string in the help output was not updated to include it.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Add "--help agent" to the category filter list in the help output
- Also add "--help agent" to the SKILL.md command map table
- Audit for other command families that may also be missing from the filter list

issues.title: FINISHED column always shows "-" in agent list, even for completed tasks

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Run ./b4w.ps1 agent list after a task completes (statusCode=200, finishTime present in JSON).

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The FINISHED column should display the completion timestamp from the finishTime field in the agent status JSON.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The FINISHED column shows "-" for all tasks, even completed ones whose JSON status contains a valid finishTime (e.g. "2026-07-27T22:57:45.635194200Z").

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The agent list table renderer either does not read the finishTime field from the task data, or the field name mismatch between the backend response and the list formatter causes it to always fall through to the "-" default.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Read finishTime from the task data and format it in the FINISHED column
- Ensure the column is populated from the same field that agent status JSON returns

issues.title: processState JSON field uses "done" while agent list STATUS uses "completed"

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Run ./b4w.ps1 agent status <id> for a completed task. Compare processState (JSON) with agent list STATUS column.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Consistent terminology between the JSON API and the CLI table output. The task spec explicitly says the deprecated label is "done".

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: JSON: processState="done", status="OK". CLI table: STATUS="completed". The JSON field processState uses "done" which is the deprecated label the task spec warns against. While the CLI STATUS column correctly shows "completed", the internal JSON field name is confusing.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The backend uses "done" as an internal process state enum value, while the CLI presentation layer maps it to "completed". The term "done" appears in user-facing JSON output which contradicts the documented deprecation of that label.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Rename the internal processState enum from "done" to "completed" to match the CLI presentation
- Or add a mapping layer so JSON output also shows "completed" instead of "done"

issues.title: agent status JSON returns verbose internal event chain in message field

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Run ./b4w.ps1 agent status <id> while a task is in progress.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The message field should contain a concise, human-readable status description.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The message field contains a long dot-separated chain of internal Java class/method names: "StatefulAgentRunner.created,PerceptiveAgent.onWillRun,PerceptiveAgent.onWillAct,ContextToAction.onWillGenerate,ContextToAction.onDidGenerate,PerceptiveAgent.onDidAct,PerceptiveAgent.onWillAct,ContextToAction.onWillGenerate". This is an internal event trace, not a user-facing message.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The backend populates the message field by concatenating internal lifecycle event handler names rather than generating a user-facing status description.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Keep the internal event chain in a separate field (e.g. eventTrace) and generate a concise human-readable message
- Or provide a summary-only mode: agent status --summary that omits the verbose message field
